operations.message: Kruskal's: process ALL edges sorted by weight ascending. Each vertex starts in its own component — notice the different colours!
Consider B–C (weight 1): B and C are in different components → ACCEPT
Accepted! Union {B} and {C}
B and C merge into one component (same colour now). Components: 4 → still need to reach 1.
MST Cost: 1
4 components remaining
Consider A–B (weight 2): A and B are in different components → ACCEPT
Accepted! Union {A} and {B, C}
A joins the B–C component. All three share a colour now.
MST Cost: 3
3 components remaining
Consider A–C (weight 3): A and C are in the SAME component → REJECT (would create cycle!)
Rejected — edge flashes red. Kruskal's skips same-component edges.
Consider B–D (weight 4): different components → ACCEPT
Accepted! D joins the A–B–C component.
D recoloured to match the main component.
MST Cost: 7
2 components remaining — just E is isolated
Consider C–D (weight 5): same component → REJECT
Rejected.
Consider C–E (weight 6): different components → ACCEPT!
Accepted! E joins. All 5 vertices now in one component.
E recoloured — entire graph is one connected component.
✓ Kruskal's MST complete! Cost = 13. Edges accepted: B–C(1) + A–B(2) + B–D(4) + C–E(6) = 13
1 component — MST spans all vertices!
